money-display.purpose: The single figure a card exists to show. Geist Mono only, tabular numerals, −0.025em. Never more than one per card.

money-inline.purpose: Table amounts, deltas, and bill figures. Same mono register, small size, so columns of money line up.

title.purpose: Page-level entry titles, including the borderless transaction title input.

body.purpose: Card eyebrows and default interface copy.

label.purpose: Buttons, field labels, table headers, muted descriptions.

micro.purpose: Uppercase 10.8px region markers (DETAILS, NOTE, OVERDUE · 1) and sidebar group names.

shadows.name: ambient-card
shadows.purpose: Resting state of cards and frame panels. Paper on paper; never more than 5% black.

shadows.name: inset-hairline
shadows.purpose: The milled edge inside inputs, buttons, and toasts, drawn by a ::before ring inset by 1px. Inverted to white at 6–8% in dark mode.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, sheets — layers that genuinely overlap content.

shadows.name: whisper-float
shadows.purpose: Toasts and stacked popovers, where the scrim and border do most of the separation.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every button. The tactile response, applied on :active only.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover and pressed fills. Hover is gated to fine pointers so touch devices never show a stuck state.

motion.name: overlay-exit
motion.purpose: Dialogs leaving — exits resolve faster than entrances.

motion.name: toast-settle
motion.purpose: Bottom-center toast stack reflowing when an item is added or dismissed.

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: Loading placeholders. The only continuous animation in the system.

motion.name: chart-shine
motion.purpose: Receipt-scanning and queue progress shimmer. Used only while a job is running.

narrative.overview:
Hoalu looks like a room built for monitoring, not for selling. Paper-white surfaces sit on a paper-white page, separated by single-pixel hairlines instead of shadows or color blocks. The room is quiet in both directions: at midday it is cool paper and graphite, at night it is a near-black slate with the same hairlines, and a third warm-paper theme shifts the whole thing toward ink and cream. Nothing in the chrome is saturated except one indigo action. The numbers are the only thing allowed to be large.

The density is the point. Type is deliberately smaller than a typical web app — body copy is 14.4px, labels are 12.6px, and the smallest micro-labels are 10.8px — so that a year of transactions, a bill schedule, and four readouts can share one screen without scrolling. Rows are 36px, cards have 16px of internal rhythm, and every table of money is set in Geist Mono with tabular figures so digits line up in a column and never jitter as values change.

The personality is restraint plus exactness. There is no gradient hero, no greeting card illustration, no icon in a pastel circle. Where a generic dashboard would reach for decoration, this system reaches for a delimiter: a hairline, an uppercase micro-label, a hatch pattern that says this value was truncated, a ≈ that says this number was converted. Precision is the aesthetic.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, bordered surfaces on a paper page; depth reserved for genuinely floating layers.
Monospace, tabular money as the only display-scale typography in the app.
One saturated signal per view; everything else is ink, ash, or hairline.
Density over comfort: 12.6px labels, 36px rows, micro-labels at 10.8px uppercase.
Three parallel worlds — cool paper, midnight, warm paper — with identical structure and different radius, ink, and accent behavior.
Honest encodings: hatched bars for clipped values, ≈ for converted amounts, asterisks for redacted ones.

rules.name: The Single Signal Rule
rules.body: Exactly one saturated, high-contrast action per view. If two controls compete for the indigo, one of them is a secondary outline.

rules.name: The Money Is Ink Rule
rules.body: Amounts are set in Graphite Ink, never tinted to show direction — the -/+ sign, the ≈ prefix, and column position carry meaning. Crimson on a number is reserved for two cases only: an overdue bill amount, and a period total that ends negative.

rules.name: The Never-Invent-A-Rate Rule
rules.body: When no exchange rate exists, show the original amount in its own currency. Never render a converted figure you had to guess, and never a ≈0.

rules.name: The Anchor-Before-Accent Rule
rules.body: A new color must earn its place in a semantic role (state, chart series, or alert) before it is used decoratively. The palette has three neutral families and does not need a fourth.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Any figure a user might compare down a column — amounts, deltas, percentages, counts, dates in tables — is Geist Mono with tabular-nums. Prose, headings, and labels are never mono. A sans-serif amount is a defect.

rules.name: The Upcase-Only-For-Markers Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for micro labels that mark a region of the interface. Never uppercase a sentence, a button, or a heading.

rules.name: The One Display Number Rule
rules.body: Each card has at most one display-scale figure. Everything else in that card is label-sized or smaller. Two 27px numbers in one card means the card is doing two jobs.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Rule
rules.body: No centered max-width container. Layout fills the viewport and the grid does the constraining; a centered column is a marketing pattern, not a ledger one.

rules.name: The Touch-First Sizes Rule
rules.body: Controls are sized for a thumb at base, then tightened for a cursor at sm and above. Growing controls only at breakpoints means desktop-sized hit areas on phones — do not do it.

rules.name: The Paper-On-Paper Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces get at most 5% black shadow. If a card looks raised, the shadow is too strong; the border should be doing the work.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Structural shadows belong exclusively to layers that overlap other content. A static card or toolbar never gets shadow-lg.

dos: Do keep one indigo action per view and make every other control an outline or ghost.
Do set every comparable figure in Geist Mono with tabular numerals; the 2xs–micro steps are correct for chips and markers.
Do reach for a 1px Slate Whisper border and 5% ambient shadow before reaching for a new fill colour.
Do use uppercase 10.8px/0.05em micro-labels to mark regions (DETAILS, NOTE, OVERDUE · 1), and nothing else.
Do encode missing certainty in the glyph: hatched bars for axis-clipped values, ≈ for converted amounts, ***** for redacted amounts, — for empty cells.
Do target 44px touch areas via the existing pointer-coarse::after pattern when a control is visually smaller than that.
Do retune the whole radius scale through --radius when theming, so shapes stay consistent across light, dark, and creamy.
donts: Don't introduce consumer-app gloss: no gradient hero cards, no icon-in-a-pastel-circle KPI tiles, no illustration or mascot inside the product chrome. This is a ledger, not a landing page.
Don't tint an ordinary amount red to mean "expense". Direction belongs to the sign; crimson belongs to overdue items, destructive actions, and periods that end negative.
Don't use a sans-serif figure anywhere a user compares values down a column.
Don't add a second display-scale number to a card, or grow body copy past 14.4px to "improve readability" — the density is a feature.
Don't use shadow-lg on static surfaces, and don't increase the resting card shadow above 5% black.
Don't centered-container the layout. Full-bleed grid only.
Don't add motion without a reduced-motion path: the system currently ships press-scale, 150–200ms transitions, and scale/opacity dialog entrances with no prefers-reduced-motion guard anywhere.
Don't wire in the dormant Redacted Script webfont for masking; redaction is literal asterisks in the money component, and that is what users already recognise.
